annotation.title_clean: Ethical Algorithms in Human-Robot-Interaction. A Proposal
annotation.title_en: Ethical Algorithms in Human-Robot-Interaction. A Proposal
annotation.venue: Computer Science & Information Technology (CS & IT), AIRCC Publishing
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical conference paper arguing autonomous robots lack human moral competence and so need ethical algorithms. It proposes a general logical form of meta-ethical arguments, grounded in the 'moral stance', as a pattern for programming ethical decision-making into robots to support trust in human-robot interaction.
key_provisions_or_claims: Trust in robots depends on reliability and human-like ethical competence.
Robots cannot take the human moral stance, so ethical algorithms must be implemented.
Proposes a logical form of meta-ethical arguments as a pattern for ethical algorithms.
Model is minimalist and not tied to a particular meta-ethical theory.
Moral demands protect common goods such as bodily integrity and autonomy.
